segments.speaker: lark
segments.text: Break the peace inside this camp, and no Scarwalker will ever speak your names again. Not your children's, either.

segments.speaker: lark
segments.text: The only road to the crater crosses the canyon, and the only bridge belongs to a goblin called Vorga. He took it in spring.

segments.speaker: lark
segments.text: His Host lets the Scarwalker caravans over to the wells, then keeps the water. A toll, he calls it. The elder has another word.

segments.speaker: lark
segments.text: Yes, he's one of Vorga's. Yes, he's a guest. No, you can't. Let the poor thing finish his tea.

segments.speaker: lark
segments.text: Young, loud, very fond of his own voice. He sends the Scarwalkers a song every new moon about how he's going to eat them.

segments.speaker: lark
segments.text: Terrible song. Good rhythm, though. And under all the shouting, he's angrier than anyone I've ever met.

segments.speaker: lark
segments.text: He knows. He's telling the whole canyon she sold the clan for a few sacks of grain, and that you're holding the leash.

segments.speaker: lark
segments.text: The lads who fought you at the ford were his. The ones who made it home haven't stopped talking about you.

segments.speaker: lark
segments.text: He knows. He doesn't sing about the Scarwalkers any more. All the new verses are about you.

segments.speaker: lark
segments.text: Whatever he thought of her, she was his grandmother. Nobody else was allowed to kill her.

segments.speaker: lark
segments.text: He says Vorga will be delighted to meet you. He says to bring rope. He seems to think that's funny.

segments.speaker: lark
segments.text: A Kindled caravan, nine days ago, under a white cloth. The elder gave them water, because the law says she must.

segments.speaker: lark
segments.text: Their leader asked after you by name. Lovely voice. Kind eyes. I didn't like how much I liked her.

segments.speaker: lark
segments.text: No. A clan has grandmothers. Vorga's Host is everyone who got tired of waiting for the grandmothers.

segments.speaker: lark
segments.text: Anything else, before the tea runs out?

segments.speaker: lark
segments.text: Nothing in the Sunscar would dare touch you tonight. Tomorrow is another song.

segments.speaker: lark
segments.text: That's the verse before the last. I've been looking for it for twenty years.

segments.speaker: lark
segments.text: Seven came home, my version goes. Hers says they came back running. Same seven, I'd wager, seen from different doorsteps.

segments.speaker: lark
segments.text: Of course not. I'd keep it too, if it were mine.

segments.speaker: lark
segments.text: Then someone else will want very badly to hear that dream. Be careful who you tell it to.

segments.speaker: lark
segments.text: Big promise. Goblins remember promises. So do songs.
